meaning:
μάστιξ, -ιγος, ἡ
[in LXX for שׁוֹט, etc. ;]
a whip, scourge: Act.22:24, Heb.11:36; metaphorically, of disease or suffering as a divine chastisement (cf. Psa.89:33, Pro.3:12, 2Ma.9:11), Mrk.3:10 5:29, 34, Luk.7:21
(AS)

elsewhere.note: For he had healed many, so that as many as had diseases pressed on him that they might touch him.
In that hour he cured many of diseases and plagues and evil spirits; and to many who were blind he gave sight.
the commanding officer commanded him to be brought into the barracks, ordering him to be examined by scourging, that he might know for what crime they shouted…
Others were tried by mocking and scourging, yes, moreover by bonds and imprisonment.
